$TSM is one of the cleanest ways to own the AI buildout because $NVDA, $AMD, $AAPL, $AVGO, $QCOM and hyperscaler custom silicon programs all depend on the same leading-edge manufacturing layer.

The real bottleneck is who has access to scarce wafer starts and TSMC remains the physical chokepoint behind almost every version of the AI trade.

With N3 capacity reportedly scaling to ~220K wafers per month, the “second source” everyone wants still doesn't really exist which means every token ultimately pays an invisible royalty to TSMC.

📺 THE SUMMER TOP MAY ALREADY BE IN + MY $AMZN & $NVDA TRADES + $SPCX WARNING AFTER FAILED MOMENTUM

The market may have already put in its seasonal summer top, and the technical picture is becoming much more challenging than the headlines suggest.

The warning signs actually started before the latest geopolitical news, when leadership stocks like $MU and $SNDK lost key moving averages, and tech began showing clear relative weakness.

*

The most important level to watch now is $SPY $740.

If buyers defend that area, the market could stage a meaningful rebound, and traders can begin reducing hedges while selectively adding exposure.

But if $SPY loses $740 and stays below it, there is little technical support until the 50-day moving average near $733, which could open the door to a much deeper pullback.

*

QQQ is already showing greater weakness than the broader market, as it tests key moving averages.

Healthy bull markets are typically led higher by tech. When tech starts leading lower instead, it raises the probability that the broader market enters a more defensive phase.

*

So, rather than making all-or-nothing bets, your focus should be on staying tactical.

Read the charts instead of reacting to every headline, adjust exposure as conditions change, and respect relative weakness when market leaders begin to fail.

*

I have a few small positions left in $AMZN and $NVDA. 

Amazon is acting somewhat better than many other tech names, while Nvidia finally showed signs of leadership after underperforming much of the semiconductor group.

Both remain tactical trades with clearly defined risk rather than high-conviction ones.

*

I'm also becoming much more cautious about $SPCX now.

The stock benefited from major Wall Street upgrades and Nasdaq-related buying, but failed to build on that momentum.

When a stock cannot rally despite overwhelmingly bullish news, that often becomes a warning signal.

Losing the key technical levels shifts the risk toward a retest of the IPO price, making disciplined risk management even more important.

Be very careful with $SPCX now.

*

Seasonally, this period often marks an important turning point.

If the market has indeed formed a summer top, you should expect more volatility, more program-driven selling, and fewer easy trend trades while institutional participation slows during the middle of summer.

*

A quick note on #crudeoil. 

Oil remains technically constructive after $USO reclaimed an important support level, suggesting buyers may still have control despite the recent geopolitical volatility.

The expectation is for a move toward the $112–114 area, where traders should consider reducing exposure into strength rather than chasing further upside.

While headlines surrounding the Middle East continue to drive short-term swings, the chart remains the primary guide, and as long as $USO holds its recent breakout, the intermediate trend remains favorable.
